stopLine: Do not modify runtime code without separate implementation authorization. Stop on unprovable process identity, guessed phone model, model-based credential merging, user-rename overwrite, device-credential schema drift, public exposure, new heavyweight runtime need, product semantics conflict, force push, release, PR, remote deletion, or external publication. Do not write delivery_integrated before the three-choice UI is removed and the new path-selection behavior plus remaining human acceptance are verified.
evidenceRefs: Current product authority records the tray-owned service lifecycle, browser-hosted Redline console, one-QR phone-to-computer binding, internal invisible transport selection, and the implementation-candidate boundary. The current three-choice pairing UI is explicitly superseded and remains an implementation delta alongside the existing human acceptance items.

DESKTOP-TRAY-WEB-CONSOLE-001 remains user_confirmed; its 2026-08-29 update keeps QR-only authorization but replaces LAN/stable-name/Tailscale user choices with one pairing QR and software-owned path selection. Automatic download, WebView2, and full native UI remain deferred.

Command scripts are wake or emergency entry points; the tray is the service-lifecycle Owner. Password removal does not open access because every phone request still requires a registered device token. Tailscale remains outside physical mDNS advertising.

Web console, QR-only session APIs, same-device origin adoption, newest-rollout selection with cached-source rediscovery and latest-user list preview, runtime identity APIs, tray Owner, packaging, and verification consumers exist in this branch as a candidate. The visible LAN/stable-name/Tailscale QR selector is now a known non-compliant implementation delta and is not delivery_integrated.

The target chain is launcher to single tray Owner to identified Node service to browser console, then one QR that binds a phone to the computer, persistent LOCALAPPDATA device identity, and software-owned LAN/stable-name/Tailscale selection and failover.

STA NotifyIcon tray, occupant classification, loopback runtime/shutdown APIs, five-area Redline console, transport discovery, portable-package identity, and main-thread tray IPC are present in source. The contract now requires collapsing the current pairing choices into one automatically selected QR while retaining transport status for diagnosis.
The implementation uses Windows PowerShell STA and WinForms already present on target Windows plus the bundled Node runtime; Electron, WebView2, online update, and new external runtimes are excluded.

Tray owns service lifecycle; runtime/tray receipts and process proof gate replacement; Unknown/Unproven occupants are fail-closed; QR is the only authorization owner and trusted-device schema/location remain unchanged.

Version/build identity comes from packaged metadata; runtime and trusted-device records live in LOCALAPPDATA; install .env retains Host/Port/LAN name but removes legacy password configuration; Redline tokens are project-owned CSS.

Existing automated checks remain the implementation baseline for QR-only authorization, repeated-scan and cross-origin identity reuse, Tailscale classification, model-first naming, device editing, routing, latest-user list preview, and duplicate rollouts. The next implementation must add one-visible-QR, automatic-path-selection, fallback, and no-duplicate-device regressions.

The newly confirmed one-QR invisible-transport delta requires separate implementation authorization before the remaining human NotifyIcon/menu, real-phone path switching, unknown-occupant comparison, and target-machine acceptance can close. Public internet, automatic download, WebView2, full native UI, release, and delivery_integrated remain deferred.
